text: Come in, come in. The spirits said you'd come. Well. They said someone would.
Sit, captain. Mind the candles. The dead are very particular about candles.
You've a lot of ghosts following you, {player}. No, don't look. They don't like it.
The house is quiet now. Lady Morrow is at rest, thanks to you. I sleep better too.
The veil's thin tonight. Speak softly.
Storms make the spirits restless. And me.

options.label: Can you really talk to the dead?

text: Lady Morrow. She waited in that house for a husband who sailed with the Meridian Fleet and never came home.
She's still waiting. The waiting has made her cruel.
Since I was seven. I heard my grandmother calling from the well. She'd been dead a year.
Mostly the dead talk about the weather and their feet. It's very disappointing.
I see water. A great deal of water. And a choice, at the end of it, that only you can make.
Gold, and a long voyage, and a betrayal by a friend who laughs too easily.
I see you eating soup. That's all. Sometimes the spirits are lazy.
Seven stones. A door at the edge of the world. And a man with a crow's name, smiling at you over a fire.
The sea is in you now. I can't see past it. That frightens me.
